Question Choices: According to the fundamental theorem of algebra, how many complex roots does a degree n polynomial have, counting multiplicity?
Hints: The degree controls the total root count.;Repeated roots count repeatedly.
Solution: It has exactly n complex roots counting multiplicity.

Question Choices: How many complex roots does a quartic (degree 4) polynomial have, counting multiplicity?
Hints: Apply the fundamental theorem of algebra.;The degree is 4.
Solution: A quartic has four complex roots counting multiplicity.

Question Choices: How many complex roots does a quadratic have, counting multiplicity?
Hints: The degree is 2.;Apply the fundamental theorem.
Solution: A quadratic has two complex roots counting multiplicity.

Question Choices: Must every real polynomial of odd degree have at least one real root? Enter Yes or No.
Hints: Complex roots come in conjugate pairs.;An odd count cannot be all pairs.
Solution: Yes — at least one root must be real.

Question Choices: A degree 5 real polynomial has roots 2i and -2i. At most how many other complex (non-real) roots can it have?
Hints: Non-real roots come in pairs.;Only one more pair fits in degree 5.
Solution: At most one more conjugate pair — 2 non-real roots.
